blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Choosing the right logistics model means accepting that B2B, B2C and e-commerce each demand very different capabilities. A single company that tries to be excellent at all three usually ends up average at each. The physical infrastructure, the staffing patterns, the technology and even the culture are simply not the same.

The differences are concrete. A company built for B2B pallets struggles with thousands of small parcels. A company built for next-day e-commerce struggles with heavy, scheduled deliveries to factories. Each model rewards a different set of strengths, and those strengths rarely transfer cleanly from one to another.

The right answer is not always to do everything in-house. Sometimes the smartest move is to outsource the model that sits furthest from your natural strength. I'd rather run one model extremely well than three models at mediocrity — and that, honestly, is the lesson most companies learn the hard way.

items.q: According to the text, what happens to a company that tries to be excellent at B2B, B2C and e-commerce at once?
options: It grows faster than its rivals
items.why: "usually ends up average at each" — tentar ser ótimo em tudo dilui a excelência.

items.q: Why does a company built for B2B pallets struggle with e-commerce?
options: It cannot handle thousands of small parcels
items.why: "A company built for B2B pallets struggles with thousands of small parcels."

items.q: What does the text suggest doing with the model that is furthest from your natural strength?
options: Run it in-house at any cost
Copy a competitor's version of it
items.why: "sometimes it is to outsource the model that sits furthest from your natural strength."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: One model run superbly beats three run poorly.
A great B2B operation will naturally excel at e-commerce too.
Different logistics models reward different strengths.
Culture and infrastructure vary from model to model.
items.why: Inferência: o texto argumenta que as forças raramente se transferem de um modelo para outro.

items.q: The phrase "the lesson most companies learn the hard way" suggests that…
options: companies usually discover this only after failing first
most companies never spread themselves too thin
the lesson is written in most textbooks
the lesson is impossible to understand
items.why: Inferência: "the hard way" = aprender por experiência dolorosa, depois de errar.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James aconselhando a empresa sobre a nova operação de e-commerce. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, the question on the table is whether we run the new e-commerce line inside the existing B2B warehouse, or set up a dedicated site for it. And I'd rather be honest with you now than optimistic today and sorry in six months.

That warehouse is superb at what it does. Pallets in, pallets out, scheduled deliveries to factories. But e-commerce is a different animal — thousands of tiny parcels, next-day promises, returns coming back every single day. The staffing pattern is different, the technology is different, and frankly the culture on that floor is different too.

If we squeeze e-commerce into the B2B site, I think we slow both of them down. The B2B team gets distracted, and the e-commerce service never really becomes excellent. So my recommendation is this: run a small pilot in a dedicated space for ninety days. Measure the cost per parcel and the on-time rate. If the numbers hold up, we commit properly. I'd prefer to test the model before we pour money into it — not after.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What decision is James helping the company make?
options: Whether to stop selling to factories
Whether to run e-commerce in the existing warehouse or a dedicated site
Whether to close the B2B warehouse
Whether to hire a new logistics director
items.why: "whether we run the new e-commerce line inside the existing B2B warehouse, or set up a dedicated site."

items.q: How does James describe the current warehouse?
options: Superb at pallets and scheduled factory deliveries
items.why: "That warehouse is superb… Pallets in, pallets out, scheduled deliveries to factories."

items.q: What does James recommend as a next step?
options: Commit fully to a dedicated site immediately
Run a ninety-day pilot in a dedicated space
items.why: "run a small pilot in a dedicated space for ninety days."

items.q: What does James imply would happen if e-commerce is squeezed into the B2B site?
options: Only the B2B side would benefit
items.why: Inferência: "we slow both of them down… the e-commerce service never really becomes excellent."

items.q: What is James's underlying attitude toward the decision?
options: Pessimistic — he thinks e-commerce cannot work
Reckless — he wants to invest heavily at once
Cautious — he wants proof before committing money
items.why: Inferência: "I'd prefer to test the model before we pour money into it — not after."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Each logistics model demands a different capability." A capability is…
options: an ability to do something well
items.why: Capability = capacidade: a habilidade de fazer algo bem.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The warehouse moves ___ efficiently, but small parcels overwhelm it."
items.why: Pallet = palete: unidade típica da operação B2B, oposta ao pequeno parcel.

items.q: "We decided to outsource the e-commerce fulfilment." To outsource means to…
options: have an external company do it
items.why: To outsource = terceirizar: contratar um parceiro externo para o serviço.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "E-commerce needs a completely different ___ — more pickers on shorter shifts."
items.why: Staffing pattern = padrão de equipe: como a mão de obra é organizada por turno.

items.q: "Running three models at mediocrity helps no one." Mediocrity means…
items.why: Mediocrity = mediocridade: qualidade apenas mediana, sem excelência.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em decisões de operações e logística. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the dedicated site." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the new e-commerce model region by region." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Operations pushed back on mixing the two flows." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar de uma proposta.

items.q: "The pilot looked good, but the team never followed through on the rollout." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; aqui, NÃO fizeram isso.

items.q: "Splitting the sites should free up capacity in the B2B warehouse." To free up means to…
items.why: Free up = liberar, tornar disponível de novo (espaço, tempo, recursos).
